title: Investigating Political and Demographic Associations in Large Language Models Through Moral Foundations Theory
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured how Large Language Models' moral reasoning on the Purity/Sanctity foundation (often linked to religious beliefs) is influenced when they are prompted to adopt personas with specific demographic attributes, including religious affiliations like Protestant, Catholic, and Atheist/Agnostic.
findings: The study found that prompting LLMs to adopt personas with detailed demographic attributes (which included religious affiliations like Protestant, Catholic, Atheist/Agnostic) resulted in significantly more extreme and stereotyped responses. This was particularly evident on the Purity and Authority moral foundations, which are often associated with religious values, causing the models' responses to diverge significantly from recorded human data and from their own baseline or explicitly prompted ideological responses.
